assumptionsReview.context: How to thread the caller's AbortSignal reason from setupTimers into MultipartAbortError without library-side synthesis (F-S-006)
assumptionsReview.choice: setupTimers reads callerSignal.reason at the moment of fire (in onCallerAbort) AND at already-aborted detection. MultipartAbortError stores reason as a readonly instance field WITHOUT embedding it into the message
assumptionsReview.rationale: Verified by Read at src/internal/timers.ts:145-150 and 187-193. The MultipartAbortError class (per Sprint 1's errors.ts and the test at parse-abort.test.ts:194-195/277-279) has a fixed message; the reason field carries the caller value verbatim. F-S-006 contract upheld. The 4 reason-variant integration tests (string/Error/undefined-arg/object) cover the contract surface.

assumptionsReview.context: FR-009 already-aborted contract surfaces via queue.signalError + iterator-loop-throw (NOT a synchronous throw at function entry)
assumptionsReview.choice: Mirror Sprint 3's pattern: validatePositiveTimeout throws inside the generator body (surfaces from first .next()); already-aborted check pushes abort error into queue (queue.signalError) — for-await loop's item.type==='error' branch then throws on first iteration
assumptionsReview.rationale: Verified by parse-multipart-related.ts:219-224 — the if-block runs after setupTimers but before listener attachment + pipe. Caller-observable behavior (first .next() rejects synchronously with MultipartAbortError) is identical to a true synchronous throw. Both T-013 tests (lines 67-87 and 89-108 of parse-abort.test.ts) verify this works. The runtime spot-check confirms .reason flows through verbatim. Async generators cannot truly throw at construction time (Sprint 3's existing T-002/T-003/T-025 contract), so this is the only correct shape. The benefit: cleanup runs through the iterator's finally exactly once, on the same path as every other error.

assumptionsReview.context: Combined-signal handler attachment timing — must be wired BEFORE pipe(); already-aborted skip-the-attach is symmetric with cleanup's removeEventListener
assumptionsReview.choice: Two cases: (a) caller signal already aborted → setupTimers stores error AND aborts controller AND does NOT install caller-signal listener (timers.ts:187-193); the parse-multipart-related-level combined-signal handler is also gated by `if (!timers.signal.aborted)` at line 244 to skip the attach when already-aborted. (b) caller signal aborts later → setupTimers' onCallerAbort listener fires, abortInternally stores error and aborts controller; combined-signal listener at parse-multipart-related-level fires once (registered with { once: true })
assumptionsReview.rationale: Verified by Read of both files. The setupTimers construction at parse-multipart-related.ts:204-211 happens BEFORE listener attachment (lines 392-397) and BEFORE pipe (line 400) — so timer-driven aborts never miss a synchronous fire. The architecture.md §3 'Layer C MUST NOT import from Layer A or B' rule is upheld (timers.ts imports only from errors.ts; parse-multipart-related.ts is the one wiring queue+timers together at the Layer A level). The abortPushed boolean at line 187/235 is belt-and-suspenders against the listener firing AFTER the synchronous already-aborted push — defensive but correct.

assumptionsReview.context: Fake-timer fixture (slowReadable with endAfterChunks flag) — does it model real network stalls?
assumptionsReview.choice: Custom Readable whose read() schedules push via setTimeout(callback, gapMs). With faked timers, advanceTimersByTimeAsync releases the setTimeouts, which lets read() push the chunk → parseMultipartRelated's 'data' listener fires → timers.resetIdle(). For idle/total tests the fixture stays silent forever (endAfterChunks=false) to model a hung connection
assumptionsReview.rationale: The fixture composes cleanly with vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['setTimeout', 'clearTimeout'] }) at every test site (verified at parse-timeouts.test.ts:193, 237, 280, 329 and parse-abort.test.ts:286). The endAfterChunks=false flag is exactly the right shape for idle-stall tests — without it, Readable.from would push EOF and trigger MultipartTruncatedError instead. Backpressure semantics: a single chunk per read() call uses dicer's natural pipe machinery; the unit tests in tests/unit/timers.test.ts also assert the contract directly without the fixture, providing a second-derivative verification. NOT cheating — this is standard vitest fake-timer testing.
